source.title: Generalization at the Edge of Stability
source.authors: M. Tuci; Caner Korkmaz; Umut Simsekli; Tolga Birdal

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including appendices, is supplied.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures correlations between its proposed sharpness-dimension quantities and empirical train–test gaps, using a different measurement framework from the listed original studies.
record.gate_note: Results on MNIST MLPs, arithmetic grokking tasks, and GPT-2 relate measured complexity to generalization or loss gaps. No experiments test random-label memorization, width beyond interpolation, convolution versus fully connected architectures, optimizer generalization rankings, or example removal. The arithmetic experiment describes grokking on a deliberately constructed task; it does not test the natural-label generalization claim in V1–V6 or V8.
record.test_reason: The study measures correlations between Hessian-spectrum or attractor-based complexity measures and train–test gaps. It does not measure V7's weight-magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance, and its own results do not test any other listed version. Citations and arguments about classical sharpness do not establish a result about magnitude-aware sharpness.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors derive a worst-case generalization bound over a random pullback attractor under explicit regularity assumptions and report that SD predicts empirical gaps across their tested settings and tracks grokking transitions. Relative performance depends on the estimator, configuration and correlation metric; these experiments do not test magnitude-aware sharpness.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies correlations between attractor-based spectral complexity measures and generalization gaps, rather than the interventions or measurements specified in the claim versions. Its empirical tasks include MNIST, arithmetic grokking, and GPT-2 on WikiText-2.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported correlation patterns vary with complexity measure, hyperparameter grouping, optimizer, and grokking configuration; SD's relative performance differs between Kendall and granulated Kendall correlations for the larger MLP.

fits_no_version.finding: SD correlates positively with train–test gaps in MNIST MLP experiments; its ranking depends on network size and whether ordinary or granulated Kendall correlation is used.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Hessian-spectrum Sharpness Dimension can correlate with generalization gaps across learning-rate and batch-size settings, with rankings dependent on the correlation metric.

fits_no_version.finding: SD tracks grokking transitions, but its trajectory can be nonmonotonic; in one configuration it rises again after test accuracy reaches 100%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sharpness Dimension reflects changes during arithmetic grokking without necessarily varying monotonically with test accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: For GPT-2 on WikiText-2, SD variants show comparatively consistent positive gap correlations, while classical sharpness has a strong negative correlation under AdamW.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Full-spectrum SD estimators can be more consistent correlates of transformer train–test gaps than classical Hessian sharpness across optimizer settings.

record.problems: The MNIST MLP correlation values in Figure 2 and Figure 3 are not fully recoverable from the supplied flattened text; the paper reports no uncertainty estimates for the empirical correlations. The GPT-2 and grokking correlation results are presented mainly as qualitative descriptions and figures. The experiments concern correlations, so they do not establish that the measured complexity causes the gap.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results bearing on V1–V8 were reported beyond the extracted gap–complexity analyses. Figure-only precise correlation cells were not reconstructed where the flattened layout did not support a secure assignment.

untested.parts: Coexistence of random-label fitting and natural-label generalization, including chance-level held-out performance with random labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity or initialization.
Held-out performance rankings of adaptive methods and SGD under specified tuning budgets.
Large-batch penalties in held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and their recovery through recipe changes. Batch-size grids alone do not report this comparison.
Effects of adding or removing dropout on held-out error.
Correlation of weight-magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance with generalization gaps, and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures among comparably fitted convolutional networks.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: T6 is relative to the supplied claim versions: the paper conducts original generalization research but measures a different construct. No verdict follows from its negative correlations for unnormalized Hessian sharpness.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization alongside natural-label test performance.
Widening past the zero-training-error threshold and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer held-out performance.
Large-batch versus small-batch held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout intervention effects on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness versus generalization gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring subsequent test accuracy.

rows.subject: 3-layer MLP
rows.operation_detail: Correlated complexity measures with empirical generalization and loss gaps over a 5 × 5 learning-rate and batch-size grid.

conditions.value: SGD, without momentum or weight decay

rows.measure: Kendall correlation between complexity measure and empirical generalization gap
rows.value: SD: 0.76; SD-SLQ: 0.76; RDS-Sharpness: -0.16; PH-Dim: -0.40; PH-Dim-Fwd: -0.21; PH-Dim-Bwd: 0.34
rows.note: The article describes qualitative ordering and gives an apparent flattened correlation matrix in the supplied text; its cell-to-measure alignment is not reliably recoverable, so the reported numbers are figure only. The actual reported result is that SD has the strongest correlation and the top RDS-Sharpness alone has weak negative correlation. This complexity–gap correlation does not measure V7's magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance.
rows.check: These complexity–gap correlations do not measure any listed version. The numerical value also needs correction: the nine-variable Figure 2 matrix gives SD-SLQ versus generalization gap as 0.61, whereas 0.76 is SD versus generalization gap. The listed PH-Dim correlations require explicit metric labels rather than a generic PH-Dim label.

rows.subject: 5-layer MLP
rows.operation_detail: Compared complexity measures' correlations with empirical generalization and loss gaps over a 5 × 5 learning-rate and batch-size grid.

conditions.value: 5-layer MLP; same training setup as 3-layer MLP

rows.measure: Kendall correlation and granulated Kendall correlation of complexity measures with generalization gap
rows.value: SD-SLQ outperforms all other indicators on Kendall τ; granulated Kendall coefficients are similar, with backward PH-Dim performing best and SD-SLQ following closely.
rows.note: The measured property is correlation of complexity measures with the gap, not magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness as in V7.
rows.check: The qualitative comparison is supported, but it evaluates alternative complexity indicators rather than V7's magnitude-aware perturbation measure. Backward PH-Dim leads on average granulated correlation; SD-SLQ leads on ordinary Kendall correlation.

rows.subject: 2-layer MLP
rows.operation_detail: Tracked complexity metrics at 100 uniformly spaced checkpoints and correlated them with the generalization gap during grokking.

conditions.value: SGD with momentum and weight decay
different learning rates, weight decay values and seeds; exact conditions shown in Figure 4

rows.measure: Correlation of complexity measures with generalization gap
rows.value: SD correlations are comparable to or higher than Eα, tr(H), and Sharpness; RDS-Sharpness performs worse than SD in all cases but the first.
rows.note: Grokking is the task's reported behavior, but the result here is correlation of complexity measures with the gap, not a test of any listed version. The text does not give the correlation values.
rows.check: The reported correlations concern SD, unnormalized Hessian sharpness, Hessian trace and trajectory complexity during grokking. None measures a listed version.

rows.subject: 3-layer MLP
rows.stage_stated: trained with SGD using only weight decay; 100 uniformly spaced checkpoints
rows.operation_detail: Tracked complexity measures through grokking and compared their behavior with test accuracy.

conditions.value: SGD with weight decay; no momentum
different learning rates, weight decay values and seeds; exact values shown in Figure 7

rows.measure: Sharpness Dimension trajectory alongside test accuracy
rows.value: The text reports SD increases while test accuracy increases slowly, sharply decreases while test accuracy increases sharply, then increases again when test accuracy reaches 100%.
rows.note: This is a trajectory association in a grokking task, not magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance as in V7.
rows.check: The increase–decrease–increase SD trajectory is explicitly reported for the first Figure 7 configuration, not uniformly across configurations. Specify learning rate 0.3, weight decay 3e-4 and Seed I for this particular finding. It does not measure magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance.

rows.subject: GPT-2
rows.operation_detail: Correlated complexity measures with empirical loss gaps over optimizer-specific hyperparameter grids.

conditions.value: SGD and SGD with momentum: 5 × 5 learning-rate and effective-batch-size grid; AdamW: 4 × 3 × 3 learning-rate, batch-size, and weight-decay grid

rows.measure: Correlation of complexity measures with empirical loss gap and 0–1 loss gap
rows.value: SD variants, especially SD-KDE and SD-PS, show the most consistent positive correlations across optimizers; classical sharpness under AdamW shows a strong negative correlation with loss gaps.
rows.note: The text reports qualitative correlation results; numeric correlations are presented in a figure without recoverable values in the supplied text. This does not compare optimizer generalization performance as V4 does.
rows.check: The qualitative result is supported. Within-optimizer correlations of complexity with loss gaps do not establish optimizer rankings in held-out performance under V4, and classical Hessian sharpness is not V7's magnitude-aware perturbation measure.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
